text.p: A strong earthquake measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale killed four people and injured at least 20 in the Venezuelan coastal city of Cumana on Wednesday, local television reported.
The Globovision network quoted Sucre state governor Ramon Martinez in Cumana. The report could not immediately be verified as telephone lines to the city were believed to be down.

Local Union Radio said Martinez had declared a state of emergency in Sucre state after the quake struck at 3.23 p.m. (1923 GMT). The U.S. Geological Survey in Golden, Colorado, said it measured 6.9 on the open-ended Richter scale.
The quake shook most of Venezuela's central and eastern coastal region and rattled office buildings in downtown Caracas. Residents made telephone calls in panic to local radio stations.

Telephone lines to the Venezuelan seismological institute FUVISIS were busy. Radio reports said the institute had placed the epicentre of the quake about 30 miles off Venezuela's eastern Caribbean coast.
The reports said the quake had toppled a wall, which fell on 60 cars on the Caribbean island Margarita and cut phone and power lines to several cities.
